response.title: Fix universe cache identity and checker error verdicts; add strict Arena gate
response.body:
Fixes two checker issues and adds reproducible regression evidence. Head `b648748`; kernel baseline `9fa2c29`. Kept draft: the resource-bounded Arena gate is not green.

### Checker changes

- Replace hash-only universe-substitution memo keys with IDs assigned after full substitution equality. Prepare the ID once per traversal instead of sorting/hashing the mapping at every expression node. Clear expression memos before recycling IDs.
- Return exit 3 for `TcError::Other` rather than reporting internal/parse errors as proof rejection. Accept/reject/decline remain 0/1/2.
- Add six cache tests, including forced hash collisions, reset safety, all expression kinds, and shared DAGs; add four CLI verdict tests.

No proof rules, `CONV_DEPTH`, declaration-name exceptions, default evaluator, main branch, or upstream Arena pin changed. The cache collision test exercises collision handling; it is not a demonstrated false-proof exploit against the old checker.

### Verification

- [Repository CI](https://github.com/sankalpsthakur/kiota/actions/runs/35532668521): passed.
- [Release tests](https://github.com/sankalpsthakur/kiota/actions/runs/35532668561): passed under both default and `KIOTA_NBE=1`; all 16 Python harness tests passed in both CI jobs.
- [Same-runner microbenchmark](https://github.com/sankalpsthakur/kiota/actions/runs/35532668537): five alternating baseline/candidate runs. Cold substitution median 214.816 ms -> 62.956 ms for 100 iterations (3.41x faster). Warm-cache median 3.728 ms -> 4.290 ms for 20,000 calls (15% slower). Synthetic substitution wall time only, not full-checker speed or Arena instruction counts. The same job verifies malformed JSON exits 1 on baseline and 3 on candidate.

### Arena gate: known failures remain

Default mode completed all 189 small tests: 70/70 invalid inputs rejected, 117/119 valid inputs accepted, two allocation failures. This matches the [unchanged-kernel baseline run](https://github.com/sankalpsthakur/kiota/actions/runs/35531839283) under identical test hashes and limits.

Failures: `perf/magma-list-deep-n36` and `perf/magma-list-pair-n21`. Both fail a 1,140,850,704-byte allocation; the deep case reaches approximately 25 million interned nodes. The gate uses a **4 GiB virtual-address-space limit and 120 s/test**, not Arena's official resource limits. It is not evidence these are newly introduced official-Arena failures. Candidate NbE sweep was still running at the last check; no full NbE pass is claimed.

The runner checkpoints each verdict, logs the active test, isolates evaluator jobs, and preserves source/binary/input artifacts before execution so runner loss cannot erase the baseline. It strips inherited diagnostic cutoffs and treats errors, declines, crashes, and timeouts as failures.

Full Mathlib acceptance, large-corpus resource fixes, and a ranking improvement remain unverified. No upstream pin bump or merge is included.

AI coding assistance was used for this change. Validation above distinguishes executed CI and benchmark results from outstanding work.

response.title: Definition can reference itself while its body is being checked
response.body:
## Summary

Kiota accepts a hand-crafted export containing an ordinary definition equivalent to:

```lean
def cutoffSelf : Sort 1 := cutoffSelf
```

The official Lean kernel rejects it because `cutoffSelf` is not available while its own body is being checked. Lean4Lean and Nanoda also reject the witness. A matched control whose body is `Sort 0` is accepted by all four checkers.

This report concerns only acceptance of this malformed declaration class; it does not make a broader claim about Kiota.

## Reproducer

Reproduced against Kiota `main` at `686063c13b22ce379c05dfe7fc03656655ac60e5` after a clean release build.

Save this as `cutoff-self.ndjson`:

```ndjson
{"meta":{"exporter":{"name":"lean4export","version":"3.1.0"},"format":{"version":"3.1.0"},"lean":{"githash":"f72c35b3f637c8c6571d353742168ab66cc22c00","version":"4.29.1"}}}
{"in":1,"str":{"pre":0,"str":"cutoffSelf"}}
{"il":1,"succ":0}
{"ie":0,"sort":1}
{"const":{"name":1,"us":[]},"ie":1}
{"def":{"all":[1],"hints":"opaque","levelParams":[],"name":1,"safety":"safe","type":0,"value":1}}
```

Then run:

```console
cargo build --release
target/release/kiota cutoff-self.ndjson
echo $?
```

Observed Kiota result: exit `0` (`ACCEPT`).

Observed official Lean 4.33 result: exit `1` (`REJECT`):

```text
while replaying declaration 'cutoffSelf':
(kernel) unknown constant 'cutoffSelf'
```

## Positive control

The control uses a distinct name and replaces the self-reference expression with `{"ie":1,"sort":0}`. Its final declaration still has `"type":0,"value":1`. Both Kiota and the official checker accept it, so the disagreement is specific to visibility of the declaration under validation rather than general file construction.

## Suspected mechanism

`handle_def_like` inserts the definition into `self.env`, then `handle_line` calls `check_last`. `check_last` constructs a checker over that environment, and `check_decl` retrieves the already-inserted declaration and validates its value in the same environment. The current declaration can consequently resolve itself while its body is inferred.

Relevant code:

- [`handle_def_like`](https://github.com/sankalpsthakur/kiota/blob/686063c13b22ce379c05dfe7fc03656655ac60e5/src/parser.rs#L248-L299)
- [definition parsing followed by `check_last`](https://github.com/sankalpsthakur/kiota/blob/686063c13b22ce379c05dfe7fc03656655ac60e5/src/parser.rs#L785-L787)
- [`check_last` constructs the checker from `self.env`](https://github.com/sankalpsthakur/kiota/blob/686063c13b22ce379c05dfe7fc03656655ac60e5/src/parser.rs#L823-L885)

## Recorded evidence

- [Investigation report](https://github.com/phiferd/lean-assurance-lab/blob/829c72e/docs/investigations/NANODA_ENV_CUTOFF_SURVIVOR.md)
- [Machine-readable upstream-main reproduction](https://github.com/phiferd/lean-assurance-lab/blob/829c72e/results/investigations/kiota-self-reference/upstream-main.json)
- [Witness](https://github.com/phiferd/lean-assurance-lab/blob/829c72e/corpus/generated/nanoda-gen-8317efea2c7d-self-reference.ndjson) and [positive control](https://github.com/phiferd/lean-assurance-lab/blob/829c72e/corpus/generated/nanoda-gen-8317efea2c7d-self-reference-control.ndjson)

response.title: Universe-parameter ownership disagreement with official Lean
response.body:
## Summary

Kiota accepts a small Lean export containing a definition whose value references
universe parameter `u`, even though that definition declares no universe
parameters. The official Lean 4.33.0 kernel rejects the same artifact with
`defnInfo invalid`. Both checkers accept a positive control that declares `u` on
the definition.

This reproduces on current Kiota `main`, revision
`686063c13b22ce379c05dfe7fc03656655ac60e5`.

I am reporting this as a validator-behavior clarification and possible
correctness issue, not as a security vulnerability. Kiota is explicitly
experimental, and the evidence below establishes only this concrete
disagreement.

## Outcomes

| Input | Official Lean 4.33.0 | Kiota `686063c` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Undeclared-universe artifact | `REJECT` (exit 1) | `ACCEPT` (exit 0) |
| Declared-universe control | `ACCEPT` (exit 0) | `ACCEPT` (exit 0) |

The final declaration in the rejected artifact is conceptually:

```text
axiom unused.{u} : Prop
def bad : Prop := unused.{u}  // bad declares no universe parameters
```

## Minimal reproducer

- [Undeclared-universe artifact](https://github.com/phiferd/lean-assurance-lab/blob/2369a10e0aa57bf70499eee77d859fa44338f8d9/corpus/minimized/nanoda-0003-auto-universe-min.ndjson), SHA-256 `6743315bd44cd3ada0eb4a23336f73eca909ecbb6202c3fff3a8068bf0df101a`
- [Declared-universe control](https://github.com/phiferd/lean-assurance-lab/blob/2369a10e0aa57bf70499eee77d859fa44338f8d9/corpus/controls/nanoda-0003-declared-const-universe.ndjson), SHA-256 `94530b9892930781b8f91bb8eb5017e444ef564084ed2b6cfd3ce0eb858faab9`

```sh
git clone https://github.com/sankalpsthakur/kiota.git /tmp/kiota
git -C /tmp/kiota checkout 686063c13b22ce379c05dfe7fc03656655ac60e5
cargo build --release --manifest-path /tmp/kiota/Cargo.toml

curl -L https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phiferd/lean-assurance-lab/2369a10e0aa57bf70499eee77d859fa44338f8d9/corpus/minimized/nanoda-0003-auto-universe-min.ndjson -o /tmp/undeclared.ndjson
curl -L https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phiferd/lean-assurance-lab/2369a10e0aa57bf70499eee77d859fa44338f8d9/corpus/controls/nanoda-0003-declared-const-universe.ndjson -o /tmp/declared.ndjson

/tmp/kiota/target/release/kiota /tmp/undeclared.ndjson
echo $?  # 0 (ACCEPT)
/tmp/kiota/target/release/kiota /tmp/declared.ndjson
echo $?  # 0 (ACCEPT)
```

The complete four-outcome machine record is
[here](https://github.com/phiferd/lean-assurance-lab/blob/2369a10e0aa57bf70499eee77d859fa44338f8d9/results/investigations/kiota-universe-ownership/upstream-main.json).

## Question and possible validation point

Should Kiota require every universe parameter occurring in a declaration's type
or value to belong to that declaration's `levelParams` list? If so, could Kiota
reject the undeclared artifact and retain the declared artifact as a positive
control?

As a source-level hypothesis only, the current `Checker::check_decl` path appears
to check duplicate declared level parameters before type/value checking, but I
did not find a traversal enforcing ownership of every occurring universe
parameter. The relevant code is
[`src/tc.rs` lines 1394-1436](https://github.com/sankalpsthakur/kiota/blob/686063c13b22ce379c05dfe7fc03656655ac60e5/src/tc.rs#L1394-L1436).

The full investigation, validator identities, and explicit non-claims are in
the [Lean Assurance Lab report](https://github.com/phiferd/lean-assurance-lab/blob/2369a10e0aa57bf70499eee77d859fa44338f8d9/docs/investigations/KIOTA_UNIVERSE_OWNERSHIP.md).

This report does not claim arbitrary false propositions can be proved through
Kiota or general Kiota unsoundness beyond this malformed declaration class.
